added_failures_note: the reviewed run carries no baseline_suite or after_suite block, so this is derived from the arm logs it cites on disk: the after arm /home/ITER/mcintos/.cache/imas-codex-saicl/logs/head-gate-final.log ends '69 passed' with EXIT=0 and no FAILED id, and the base arm /home/ITER/mcintos/.cache/imas-codex-saicl/logs/negative-control.log ends '3 failed' with EXIT=1 whose ids are the three new guard tests at the base revision; no failure is added at the head.

findings.text: non-blocking: assert f"VERDICT=clean {warmup_state}" in result.stdout compares the child's output against the same warmup_state the test itself interpolated into that child's script, so both sides move together and the assertion holds whenever the returncode is zero; the guard's real teeth are the child's sys.modules assertions reached through line 147, and this line adds no independent failure condition.

non-blocking: test_help_imports_no_command_module asserts only the fourteen command modules via _loaded_from(_DEFERRED_MODULES), while the done_when requires a test to fail when the language-model client library or the schema runtime is imported 'by the time imas-codex --help exits'; no assertion covers litellm, imas_codex.graph or linkml_runtime on the help path, so that half of the clause has no guard even though the measured 0.13 s help start implies those imports are absent.

non-blocking: the method field claims the warm arm pre-imports imas_codex.llm.server 'so warmup.start() has already run before the guard's own subprocesses', but the guard spawns a fresh interpreter per run via _run_fresh_interpreter, which inherits no sys.modules, so every run starts its own warm-up; the cold and warm arms therefore assert against the same child-process state and the twenty runs do not measure the cross-state stability the record claims.

non-blocking: attribution.base_named_parts_seconds is 7.11 s, but the same record's base steps have incrementals 5.583 + 0.501 + 1.101 + 0.402 = 7.587 s and a cumulative median of 7.616 s, so the committed figures do not yield the stated 7.11 s and the named parts exceed the 7.25 s whole start they are subtracted from; differencing medians of separate cumulative runs is not a valid decomposition, so the 98.1 % headline cannot be re-derived from the record that states it.

non-blocking: the 'Named parts, cumulative' row reads 7.11 s while the five rows above it in the same table sum to 0.03 + 5.58 + 0.50 + 1.10 + 0.40 = 7.61 s, so the table contradicts itself and the 98.1 % prose at line 24 rests on the number its own rows do not support.

non-blocking: the committed records and startup-timing-parts.py point their new arm at a .reckon-worktrees path and their base arm at ~/.cache/imas-codex-saicl/base-tree, both of which are reclaimed, so the re-derivability the fragment promises fails as soon as either is cleaned up and a later reader can only read the numbers, not regenerate them.

non-blocking: the comment correction is in a file that appears in neither the declared write paths nor the reopen's granted_paths, and the resume advice named only the server and sn_tools comments; the manifest discloses it under scope_note, but the scope was not extended before the write.

non-blocking: the new comment reads 'the warm-up threads import modules concurrently, and iterating sys.modules... iterate a copy so the verdict is stable' — the ellipsis breaks the sentence, so the reason the snapshot exists is not stated in prose a reader can follow.

non-blocking: the reported fleet-node five met the 15 s bound only after being re-taken at load 28-32; the earlier five at load 37-48 produced a 15.61 s start and a 13.14 s median, so the bound holds at the quieter load and is missed at the load the base arm was timed at (48.5), and the html states this but the comparison pairs a load-48 base against a load-28 change.
